summary: The agent completed a substantial implementation, but both baseline and new suites failed during a clean compile because the processor generated invalid Java for an existing type-annotated array attribute.
quick_failure_summary: Generated `.class` literals include type-use annotations, causing value-fixture compilation to fail before tests run.

details.reasoning: In `ValueAttribute.binaryCodec`, array codecs are generated with `component.toString() + ".class"`. For the existing `HasTypeAnnotation.bte()` declaration, javac's type string contains type-use annotations, so the processor emits `@TypeA,@TypeB byte.class`, which is invalid Java. The clean verifier build reports four syntax errors in `ImmutableHasTypeAnnotation.java` and stops before Surefire, accounting for all 326 baseline and 38 new test failures. This is best classified as FAIL_SYNTAX_ERROR because the agent's generated source cannot compile.
details.secondary_factors: The implementation also regressed the baseline fixture module. The agent's final broad validation did not clean `value-fixture`; its trajectory shows Maven compiling only one Java 17 source there and treating the other classes as up to date, so stale generated outputs masked the defect. The focused clean build covered only the serial module and the agent's own fixtures, which did not include a type-annotated array.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is broad and appropriately difficult but demonstrably solvable by the reference implementation. The verifier failure is a deterministic clean-compilation regression in an existing fixture, not an undocumented behavioral expectation. Although type-use annotations are not singled out in the prompt, maintaining compilable output for existing source declarations is a normal baseline requirement and the relevant fixture was visible in the repository.

evidence: `junit_base.xml` records 326/326 failures and `junit_new.xml` records 38/38 failures because Maven failed before Surefire reports were produced.

The verifier log consistently reports javac syntax errors at generated `ImmutableHasTypeAnnotation.java` lines 170 and 179: `illegal start of expression` and `no annotations are allowed in the type of a class literal`.
The generated source contains `Binary.arrayCodec(Binary.BYTE_CODEC, @TypeA,@TypeB byte.class)`, directly matching the agent patch's use of `component.toString()` when constructing a class literal.
The visible baseline source `value-fixture/src/org/immutables/fixture/HasTypeAnnotation.java` declares `public abstract @TypeA @TypeB byte[] bte()`.

The trajectory shows the agent's broad command was `./mvnw -pl generator-fixture,value-fixture -am test -DskipTests` without `clean`; Maven then compiled only one value-fixture source and reported other classes up to date, so the apparent success was not an infrastructure failure.
No API outage, missing dependency, permission failure, verifier crash, or shared bootstrap failure appears in the trajectory or test artifacts.
environment_assessment.finding: No external blocker was found; clean-build coverage should be used when validating annotation-processor changes to prevent stale generated sources from hiding syntax regressions.
